about.title: My Story
about.text_short: I am a biologist and researcher. I spent years in labs such as CBM-CSIC and Universität Konstanz learning that a result only counts if it is reproducible. Along the way I discovered that Data Science and AI are the best tools I know for solving complex problems, and today I build end-to-end products with them, such as Sextant IA, which is already in production.
about.lead: I did not come to data because it was trendy. I came because, as a scientist, I needed better tools to find answers.

chapters.title: Chapter 1 · Learning to doubt
chapters.text: It all started at the University of Salamanca and continued at the Severo Ochoa Centre for Molecular Biology, studying how bacteria repair their DNA. There I learned the most valuable lesson of my career: a data point is not a truth until you have questioned, replicated and understood it. My first scientific publication (Biomolecules, 2020) was born from that discipline.

chapters.title: Chapter 2 · When data outgrows the lab
chapters.text: At Universität Konstanz (Germany) I faced a different challenge: experiments produced more information than one person could analyse by hand. I started working on HPC clusters with Slurm, assembling transcriptomes de novo and applying multivariate statistics, while studying a Master's in Bioinformatics and Biostatistics. That was when I understood that code could be an extension of the scientific method.

chapters.title: Chapter 3 · Rigor at scale
chapters.text: Back at CBM-CSIC I took over the lab's computational strategy: reproducible pipelines over more than 1 TB of genomic data, mentoring 8 junior researchers and managing sequencing providers. When a key dataset was degraded by a hardware failure, I designed a hybrid strategy to rescue it. That project, and two others, ended up as peer-reviewed publications. I learned that engineering also means looking after people and data when things go wrong.

chapters.title: Chapter 4 · AI as the ultimate tool
chapters.text: I wanted to go beyond analysis and build solutions. I completed a Master's in Data Science & AI, evaluated AI models through RLHF and, above all, set out to create Sextant IA: an intelligent travel planner that I designed, developed and shipped to production end to end. Today I bring the same rigor I learned with a pipette to every model, every prompt and every line of code.

about.closing: Above all, I am still a scientist: curious, methodical and eager to learn from the people around me. It is just that now my experiments also get deployed to production.

value_proposition.title: What I bring to a team

points.title: Rigor and reproducibility
points.description: Trained in the scientific method: traceability, statistical validation and no shortcuts. A result that cannot be reproduced is not a result.

points.title: End-to-end execution

points.title: Bridge between science and business

experience_section.title: Experience
experience_section.intro: Every stage has taught me something different. This is the story of what I have built and what I learned building it.

featured.story: Sextant IA was born from two passions: travelling and discovering the history of every place. I set out to build an assistant that does not just list destinations, but understands each traveller's preferences and designs a meaningful trip. I owned the project end to end: architecture, LLM-orchestrated backend, Django frontend, deployment and release to production.
featured.production_note: The Sextant IA website is built, published and running in production. It is my clearest proof that I can take an idea from concept to a real product in users' hands.
impact: An engine that turns user preferences into a complete itinerary and dynamically breaks it down into daily plans.
Automatic enrichment with cultural and historical context for every location.
Full end-to-end cycle: design, development, deployment and maintenance of the production website.

items.story: Before building with AI, I wanted to understand how it is evaluated from the inside. I produced strict ground truth for search and computer vision algorithms, helping fine-tune models through RLHF. I found that my scientific training fitted naturally: evaluating a model is, at heart, designing a good experiment.
impact: Quality assurance for predictive and recommendation models.
Thorough analytical documentation for continuous accuracy improvement.

items.company: Severo Ochoa Centre for Molecular Biology (CBM-CSIC-UAM)
items.story: Here I took over the lab's computational strategy. I designed reproducible Python and Bash pipelines for more than 1 TB of genomic data, and learned that leading also means teaching: I guided 8 junior researchers through their first steps. When a Nanopore dataset was degraded by a hardware failure, I did not give it up for lost: I designed a hybrid strategy with Illumina that saved the project.
impact: Mentored 8 junior researchers (BSc, MSc and technicians).
Significantly reduced computing times through parallelisation with GNU Parallel.
Rescued a high-cost genomic dataset (ONT + Illumina).

items.story: Moving to Germany was both a professional and a personal leap. I owned the full data lifecycle: from experimental design and bioreactors to statistical analysis on HPC clusters. It was the first time data volume forced me to think like an engineer, and I discovered I loved it.
impact: De novo assembly of eukaryotic transcriptomes from environmental samples.
Multivariate analysis of communities in oligotrophic ecosystems.

projects_section.title: Projects
projects_section.intro: Every project started with a concrete problem. This is how I approached them.

items.title: Sextant IA
items.challenge: Planning a tailor-made trip takes hours of scattered research and rarely includes the historical or cultural context that gives each place its meaning.
items.approach: I designed a backend that orchestrates LLMs to generate a main itinerary, break it down into daily plans and enrich it with cultural information, all served from a Django frontend.
items.result: A public website, deployed and in production: a real product built end to end.

items.title: Genomic Data Rescue in Leishmania
items.challenge: A high-cost Nanopore sequencing experiment was degraded by a hardware failure, putting the redefinition of Leishmania donovani genome annotations at risk.
items.approach: I designed a hybrid strategy using high-fidelity Illumina reads to correct the transcriptome, with scripts parallelised via GNU Parallel to analyse Ribo-Seq data.
items.result: Project saved and published in Genes (2023), DOI 10.3390/genes14081637.

items.title: Proteogenomics of Leishmania donovani
items.challenge: The Leishmania donovani reference genome did not capture every protein the parasite actually produces.
items.approach: I integrated mass spectrometry data with genome annotations and statistically validated the candidate coding sequences.
items.result: Identification of previously unannotated proteins, published in Genes (2024), DOI 10.3390/genes15060775.

items.title: DSMarket: Retail Forecasting
items.challenge: A retailer with more than 3,000 products needed to anticipate demand and understand its customers to optimise inventory.
items.approach: I cleaned 5 years of transactions (500K+ records), segmented customers with K-Means and trained Lasso Regression models for forecasting.
items.result: 6 actionable customer segments and an executive Power BI dashboard for inventory decisions.

items.title: Environmental transcriptomics in aquatic ecosystems
items.challenge: Analysing microbial communities in nutrient-poor lakes produced data volumes impossible to process locally.
items.approach: I set up hybrid local/HPC workflows with Slurm to assemble transcriptomes de novo and applied multivariate statistics.
items.result: Efficient use of limited computing resources and robust community analysis.

items.certification: Daily professional use (2 years in Germany)
